content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends the development of a structured hypoglycemia prevention plan. This plan should include a detailed assessment of the patient’s medical history, evaluation of cognitive function, re-evaluation of current treatment regimens, and the prescription of glucagon when deemed appropriate. Key components of this prevention plan include regular and thorough assessments of the patient’s history of hypoglycemia, their level of hypoglycemia awareness, and the need for continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Structured patient education is also a critical element of the plan, with a particular focus on improving hypoglycemia awareness. Special emphasis is placed on educating individuals who have impaired hypoglycemia awareness or those who experience recurrent episodes of hypoglycemia, as these groups are at higher risk and require targeted interventions.
